llm.summary: The skill is an instruction-only, self-contained Chinese-language mental-health support guide whose requested resources and instructions align with its stated purpose — it contains no installs, no env/credential requests, and no hidden endpoints.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (clinical psychological support, crisis intervention, CBT, referrals) match the provided SKILL.md and the many reference documents. There are no binaries, credentials, or unrelated requirements (e.g., cloud keys) that would be out of scope for a mental-health support assistant.

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are self-contained guidance, assessment scales, scripts, and crisis workflows. They reference only the included local reference files. There are no instructions to read unrelated system files, call external APIs, or exfiltrate data. The only external endpoints mentioned are public emergency hotlines (telephone numbers) which are appropriate for crisis response guidance.

llm.guidance: This skill is internally coherent and appears to be what it claims: a static set of clinical guidance, assessment tools, crisis scripts and ethics. Before installing, consider: (1) jurisdiction and coverage — hotlines and emergency numbers are China-centric (12356, 400-161-9995, regional numbers); if you serve users outside that region update/localize resources; (2) legal/operational risk — the skill is explicit that it is not a diagnostic or medical service and includes ethics about breaking confidentiality for imminent harm, but you should ensure your deployment environment and policies handle crisis escalations appropriately (e.g., who will act when the assistant identifies high suicide risk); (3) accuracy and update responsibility — references DSM/ICD and other sources but verify those references meet your local clinical/legal standards; (4) privacy — README asserts no data is sent externally, but confirm the host/agent runtime policy (logging, transcripts, backups) matches your privacy needs; (5) supervision — this tool is guidance-only; consider adding disclaimers and a path to human clinician escalation in your product. If you need the skill to operate in other countries, prepare localized crisis contacts and legal guidance.
